title: How we can help | English-speaking psychologists for work and life in Italy – Blooming
description: Career coaching & guidance, workplace coaching, psychological support and psychotherapy online, with psychologists who work together. For people living in Italy or moving here. Free first meeting.

data.title: Four kinds of help, from a job search that's stalled to a hard time far from home.

p.t: Blooming's psychologists work online, by video call, with people living in Italy or about to move here. Work and the rest of your life don't run on separate tracks, so career help and psychological help sit in the same small practice.

data.title: Careers and work on one side, hard times and deeper difficulties on the other.

p.t: You don't need to know which one fits before you get in touch. Working that out is part of the free first meeting.

items.title: Career coaching & guidance
items.who: With a psychologist · over ten years in HR

p.t: Perhaps you've sent application after application and can't even get an interview, or your partner's job brought you to Italy and your own career has been on hold ever since. The psychologist you work with has spent over ten years in HR and knows the Italian job market. She works with you on your CV, where and how to look, interviews, and building contacts on LinkedIn and beyond. You can also take stock of your skills, choose a direction when none looks obvious, decide whether a course is worth it, or go through a job offer before you negotiate. She'll also give you a realistic idea of how much Italian the roles you want are likely to need.

Nobody can promise you a job; your psychologist helps you prepare and decide, including when months of rejections start to wear you down. Recognition of a foreign qualification is a separate process run by other bodies, and in the meantime she can help you decide what to do with your experience.

items.title: Workplace coaching
items.who: With a psychologist · over ten years in HR

p.t: Having a job doesn't mean work is going well. Every meeting may be in Italian, and you come home exhausted from following it and from never quite saying what you meant. Or a conflict with a colleague has dragged on for months, or a reorganisation you didn't ask for has changed your role. In coaching, the psychologist works with you on stress, on relationships with colleagues and managers, and on getting things done without running yourself into the ground. It also covers finding your motivation again when you feel stuck, leading a team for the first time and planning your next step at work. If the question becomes whether to stay or move on, that's career guidance, with the same psychologist.
Coaching isn't therapy. If something heavier comes up, she will tell you and can suggest working with one of our psychotherapists.

items.title: Psychological support

p.t: Hard things don't wait until you feel settled. A parent at home becomes seriously ill, physically or mentally, and you're managing from a distance, between calls and flight searches. Someone you love dies and you can't easily be there. A relationship ends, or the job that brought you here does. Trying for a baby means tests and appointments in a language you're still learning, and a new baby arrives with your own family a long flight away. Even the move itself can turn out heavier than you expected.
Your psychologist is also a psychotherapist and has worked in hospitals, clinics and private practice. She has an MSc in work and organisational psychology too.

items.title: Psychotherapy

p.t: Some difficulties were there long before the move; others started after it, far from the people who know you best. You might lie awake going over everything that could go wrong, or feel flat and far away for weeks at a time. Some people find they keep checking or repeating things they can't stop. For others, food has become a battle, or something they can't cut down has started to run their days. You may notice the same patterns in your relationships again and again, or still be living with something that happened to you years ago.

Psychotherapy is for difficulties that run deep or have lasted a long time. Your therapist works in a cognitive behavioural way and looks at your body, your mind and your circumstances together, including the distance from home.

data.title: Some changes hit your work and your home life at once.

p.t: Moving country and working remotely are two of them. Each one touches more than one area, which is where having career help and psychological help in the same practice is useful.

items.title: Moving to Italy

p.t: You came for a job, for love or for a fresh start, or you're about to arrive. Perhaps you followed your partner and your own work is the part still waiting. The paperwork is exhausting, and the practice can't do it for you. What it can help with is what the move does to your work and to how you feel.
Work.

In career guidance you look at where your experience fits here and what to change in your CV. Your psychologist can help you build contacts when you hardly know anyone yet, and give you a sense of how much Italian your field asks for.
Settling in.

Loneliness can creep up in the months when nobody calls you by name. Missing people at home, or feeling slow and awkward in every conversation, can wear you down even when the move was your choice. Psychological support helps with the strain of settling in.
The language is a common hurdle: 60% of expats in Italy find it hard to live here without speaking Italian.
If you're coming back after years abroad and would rather read in Italian, there's a version of this page for you:

p.t: Your employer might be in London or Berlin, your team a row of faces on a screen, and outside the window a town you're still getting to know. Because the laptop never leaves the kitchen table, the working day spills into the evening. Some weeks the only conversations you have are on calls.

Workplace coaching can help you put some shape back into your days, and think about where your career goes from here if working alone has left you unsure. The loneliness is something to talk through in psychological support.

data.title: When work and life tangle, your coach and your therapist can work together.

p.t: Say your job search has dragged on for months. You're working on applications in career coaching, but the rejections have started to affect your sleep and your confidence. Your coach can suggest a few sessions with one of our psychotherapists alongside the career work. It can go the other way too. A hard time at home can make work feel impossible, and once things are steadier, your therapist can suggest career coaching to help you get back on track at work.
With your consent, your coach and your therapist can talk to each other.

data.title: Psychologist, psychotherapist and coach do different jobs.

p.t: In Italy, psychologists are registered with the Order of Psychologists. Psychologists can offer psychological support and career guidance. The psychologists at this practice are registered.

items.note: Scope: to verify with a source.

p.t: A psychotherapist is a psychologist or doctor with at least four years of specialist training in psychotherapy. At this practice, psychotherapy is offered by a cognitive behavioural psychotherapist.

items.note: Training length: to verify. Monica's year of specialisation: to confirm.

p.t: Coaching isn't a regulated profession in Italy, so coaches come from many different backgrounds. At this practice, coaching is done by a registered psychologist.

items.note: Regulation: to check with your own adviser.

p.t: A problem at work doesn't automatically call for therapy, and a hard time doesn't always need months of sessions.

data.title: The first meeting is free, lasts 30 minutes, and there's no obligation to continue.

p.t: It's a video call, online from anywhere in Italy or before you arrive. It isn't a session. You say what's going on and find out whether the practice can help, and how.
When you book, choose what you need. If you're not sure, pick "Not sure yet", and in the meeting you work out together which path to take.

If you decide to go on, you plan the next steps with the psychologist you met. If it doesn't feel right, you can say so and stop there; if what you need fits another area, you can carry on with a colleague. If you decide not to go on, we won't contact you again.
